context: Analyze the supplied deadlock snapshot; it is the complete data for this problem, so no external API, file, or additional information is needed. Locks are exclusive and non-reentrant. Each thread keeps all held locks while waiting and requests at most one additional lock. Build a wait-for edge waiter -> holder labeled by the requested lock exactly when a thread requests a lock currently held by another thread (or by itself, a self-cycle); a null waiting_for or a request for an unowned lock creates no edge. can_abort is explicit and never inferred from cost, blocking, or cycle membership; a protected thread can never be a victim. Rollback of a victim releases ALL locks that victim currently holds; it does not assign released locks to waiters and does not simulate future scheduling. After choosing victims, recompute remaining wait-for edges from surviving threads using their original requests and the surviving owners. A complete recovery must leave no directed cycle. If any cycle has no abortable member, status is unrecoverable_under_model and plan/total_rollback_cost are null (never a partial plan). Otherwise minimize the exact total rollback cost; among equal-cost sets choose the lexicographically smallest sorted victim list. Because every thread has out-degree at most one, cycles are disjoint and the cheapest eligible member of each cycle (smallest ID on equal cost) is the optimal recovery; you may enumerate all subsets of abortable threads to verify the global tie-break. Cycle lists are rotated to their lexicographically smallest thread ID in edge direction, without repeating the closing member, and cycles are sorted lexicographically. cycle_members and blocked_behind_cycles are sorted lexicographically; blocked_behind_cycles are non-cycle threads whose wait chain reaches a cycle. All wait-for edges (original and remaining) are sorted by (waiter, holder, lock); victims and released_locks are sorted lexicographically. No deadlock uses empty victims/released lists, total_rollback_cost 0, and remaining_edges identical to the original edges. The snapshot field must echo the input exactly, preserving list order. IDs are opaque case-sensitive strings; use Python's case-sensitive lexicographic order (no numeric-aware sorting). Use exact decimal integers for costs. The explanation must be exactly one of these templates: 'No deadlock: the snapshot has no directed cycle; no rollback is needed (total cost 0).', 'Rollback <victims in sorted order, comma-space separated> for total cost <cost>; release <released locks in sorted order, comma-space separated> to break every current cycle.', or 'Unrecoverable under this model: at least one cycle has no abortable member; no complete plan or cost is available.'
